moments.title: Jenney designs a new kind of tower
moments.text: William Le Baron Jenney designed an office building for the Home Insurance Company that carried its weight on an iron and steel frame instead of thick load-bearing walls.

moments.title: Ten stories at LaSalle and Adams
moments.text: The building was finished at 10 stories and about 138 feet tall. It is widely called the first skyscraper, though historians still debate the title.

moments.title: Two more stories
moments.text: Two stories were added to the top of the building.

moments.title: Torn down
moments.text: The building was demolished to make way for a much larger tower on the same corner.

moments.title: The Field Building rises
moments.text: The 45-story Field Building, by Graham, Anderson, Probst & White, was finished on the site. It was named a Chicago Landmark in 1994.

moments.title: Today: 135 S. LaSalle St
moments.text: The Field Building, also known as the LaSalle Bank Building, still stands. A city landmark plaque notes that the Home Insurance Building once stood here.

facts.label: Frame
facts.note: Among the first buildings to use structural steel in its frame.

sources.title: Lost Legends #12: The Home Insurance Building (Preservation Chicago / Chicago YIMBY)

checked.notes: Jenney design, built 1884 to 1885, 10 stories and 138 feet, two stories added 1891, demolished 1931 for the Field Building (completed 1934; Chicago Landmark Feb 9, 1994) confirmed (Wikipedia, City of Chicago Landmarks). The 'first skyscraper' title is a common view rather than a settled fact; the story already says 'often called'. One source gives 1932 for the demolition; 1931 is kept.
